results.input: A notary ran away with money he was holding. Whose property was it, and what did the family then find out about that fortune?
results.reply: That was the fortune of the widow Dubuc — Charles's first wife, the one before me, though I only heard all this told afterward. A notary at Ingouville, who held her property, went off one fine day with all the money in his office. Then the family looked into it, and what did they find? That the good lady had lied! The house at Dieppe was eaten up with mortgages, no one knew what she had really placed with the notary, and her famous share in the boat was worth barely a thousand crowns — after all the trumpeting about her riches.

results.input: In the early days at Tostes, when Charles rode away in the morning, what did you do from your window?
results.reply: I would stay at the window in my dressing gown, between the two pots of geraniums, and call down to him while he buckled his spurs at the mounting stone.
